iut_type: End Product (BLE+USB dual-mode keyboard, Topre Corporation)
customer_question: Do we absolutely need to Pass every test item that came back Fail or Indecisive, in order to get our certification?
question_variants: Is there any way to get certified without resolving the Fail/Indecisive PTS results?
actual_issue: Several PTS test items for BAS and HIDS came back Fail or Indecisive, and the customer wanted to know whether registration could still proceed without resolving them, given development/schedule pressure to finish certification by end of August.
plain_english_explanation: For a profile-implementing product, all assigned test items must Pass before certification/registration can proceed — Fail or Indecisive results block registration. As a last-resort alternative if the missing functionality (BAS/DIS/HIDS) genuinely isn't used by the product in practice and no market compatibility issues exist, the customer could instead formally reference an existing certified module's Profile Subsystem registration (e.g., a Nordic QDID already covering BAS, DIS, and HIDS) rather than fixing their own software, but this was framed explicitly as a fallback 'escape route,' not a primary recommendation, and the customer was encouraged to first pursue software remediation.
consultant_answer: Yes — for a profile-having product, registration requires Passing all assigned test items; Fail or Indecisive results block certification. As a last-resort fallback only, if your existing non-BAS/DIS/HIDS keyboard model has had no market compatibility problems (meaning those features aren't actually used), you could instead formally reference an already-certified module's Profile Subsystem registration that includes those profiles (e.g., a specific Nordic QDID) instead of fixing your own software — but we recommend pursuing the software fix first and treating this only as a final fallback.
decision_logic: Profile-implementing product registrations require full Pass results on all assigned test items; referencing an unrelated third-party module's already-certified Profile Subsystem registration is a legitimate but secondary fallback path when the product's actual real-world feature usage doesn't depend on resolving the failing items through software fixes.
final_recommendation: Present the reference-registration fallback only after first encouraging genuine software remediation, and only when the customer can confirm the relevant feature isn't actually exercised in their shipping product.
risk_if_done_wrong: Treating the reference-registration fallback as a default solution rather than a last resort could result in registrations that don't accurately reflect the product's actual implemented behavior.
